tip.behind: **{0}** · {1} new commit(s) on {2} — click to pull them in
tip.mergeReady: **{0}** · all conflicts fixed — finish the merge
tip.noUpstream: **{0}** · branch {1} isn't linked to a remote yet
notify.sameFile: Heads up! {0} changed the same file(s) you're working on: {1}. Pulling now keeps the conflict small.
pull.okLocal: Merged! Got {0} commit(s) from your team — your own work is all still here.
pull.ok: Merged! Got {0} commit(s) from your team.
pull.upToDate: You already have the latest code. Nothing to pull.
pull.mergeConflict: Your commits and your teammate's changed the same lines in {0} file(s). Pick what to keep in each file, save, then press “Finish merge”.
pull.mergeConflictStash: Your uncommitted work is parked safely and comes back right after the merge is finished.
pull.autostashConflict: Your teammate's code is in, but it overlaps work you haven't committed yet in {0} file(s). Don't worry — a backup of your work is kept until you're done. Fix the files, then stage them.
pull.blocked: There are still {0} unresolved file(s) from last time. Finish those first, then pull again.
pull.blockedReady: Conflicts are fixed but the merge isn't finished yet. Press “Finish merge” first.
pull.noUpstream: This branch isn't linked to a remote yet. Push it once (Source Control → “Publish Branch”) and PushPal will start watching it.
pull.detached: You're not on a branch right now (detached HEAD). Switch to a branch, then pull.
pull.untracked: You have new file(s) with the same name as file(s) your teammate just added: {0}. Rename or move yours, then try again.
err.auth: Couldn't sign in to the remote. Press Sync once in Source Control to log in, then PushPal can check again.
err.network: Can't reach the remote right now (offline?). PushPal will keep trying.
err.identity: Git doesn't know your name yet. Set user.name and user.email, then try again.
err.locked: Another git command is running (index.lock). Wait a moment and try again.
err.notRepo: This folder is no longer a git repository.
autostash.dropped: All files are fixed — PushPal cleaned up the backup stash for you.
merge.ready: All conflicts in {0} are fixed. Press “Finish merge” to save the merge.
merge.finished: Merge finished. You're up to date!
noRepo: Open a folder that uses git to let PushPal watch it.

test.body: If you can see this, notifications work! 👋
test.sentInVSCode: This is how PushPal will tell you inside VS Code.
desktop.unavailable: Desktop notifications aren't available on this computer, so PushPal will use VS Code pop-ups.
desktop.osascript: Using basic macOS notifications (no buttons). Install alerter for “Pull in changes” buttons that stay on screen.
bg.enabled: PushPal will now check for new code every minute, even when VS Code is closed.
bg.disabled: Background checking is off. The background task has been removed.
bg.unsupported: Checking while VS Code is closed is available on macOS and Windows only.
bg.failed: Couldn't set up the background task: {0}
welcome.prompt: PushPal is ready. Want a 1-minute setup?
setup.title: PushPal Setup
alerter.installing: Installing alerter in the terminal. When it finishes, press “Send test” again.
alerter.noBrew: alerter is installed with Homebrew. Install Homebrew first (brew.sh), then try again.
wv.welcome.title: Hi! I'm Pal from PushPal
wv.welcome.body: When a teammate pushes new code, I'll tell you right away and pull it into your project in one click — without losing your work.
wv.welcome.f1: Know the moment a teammate pushes
wv.welcome.f2: Pull in their code with one click
wv.welcome.f3: Your work stays safe; conflicts come with a guide
wv.lang.title: Which language do you prefer?
wv.lang.body: You can change it any time in Settings.
wv.lang.thHint: เป็นกันเอง อ่านง่าย
wv.theme.title: Pick a look
wv.theme.body: Applies to every PushPal screen. Preview it below.
wv.theme.systemHint: Switches with your VS Code theme
wv.notify.title: How should I let you know?
wv.notify.body: Pick as many as you like.
wv.notify.vscodeHint: A pop-up in the corner while you're coding.
wv.notify.desktopHint: A system notification when you're in another app. If VS Code is in front, you only get the VS Code pop-up — never both.
wv.notify.background: Even when VS Code is closed
wv.notify.backgroundHint: I'll set up a small background task on this computer that runs git fetch once a minute. It never changes your files, and turning it off removes it.
wv.notify.backgroundWin: Uses Windows Task Scheduler (no pop-up windows).
wv.notify.backgroundNo: Available on macOS and Windows only.
wv.test.title: Let's test a notification
wv.test.body: Press the button and look at the corner of your screen.
wv.test.vscodeOnly: Sent inside VS Code. Desktop notifications aren't available on this computer.
wv.test.mac2: Find “Visual Studio Code” (or “alerter”) and turn on Allow notifications
wv.test.mac3: Set the alert style to Persistent so it stays until you click
wv.test.macNoAlerter: For buttons like “Pull in changes” right on the notification, install the small free helper alerter.
wv.test.alerterOk: alerter is installed — notifications will have buttons.
wv.test.win2: Make sure notifications are on for “Visual Studio Code” (or “Windows PowerShell”)
wv.test.win3: Turn off Do not disturb / Focus while you work with your team
wv.test.linux1: PushPal uses notify-send. Install the libnotify package if nothing shows up.
wv.test.linux2: Turn off Do not disturb in your desktop's notification settings
wv.done.title: All set!
wv.done.tip1: Look at the bottom-left status bar: it turns yellow when teammates push. Click it to pull their code in.
wv.done.tip2: Click Pal in the Activity Bar for “My Team”: the timeline, conflicts and help.
wv.done.tip3: Run “PushPal: ตั้งค่าใหม่” from the Command Palette to see this setup again.
wv.team.noRepo.title: No git project open yet
wv.team.noRepo.body: Open a project folder that uses git, or clone one from GitHub. I'll keep an eye on it for you.
wv.team.upToDateSub: I'll tell you the moment a teammate pushes.
wv.team.pullingSub: Your own work is set aside safely while this runs.
wv.team.successSub: Got {0} commit(s). Your own work is all still here.
wv.team.sameFileBody: {0} changed files you're editing too. Pull now to keep conflicts small.
wv.team.noUpstream.title: This branch isn't on GitHub yet
wv.team.noUpstream.body: Publish branch “{0}” once and I'll start watching it for teammates' pushes.
wv.team.detached.title: You're not on a branch
wv.team.detached.body: Switch to a branch (like main) and I'll start watching it.
wv.team.error.title: I couldn't check just now
wv.team.conflict.merge: Your commits and your teammate's changed the same lines
wv.team.conflict.autostash: Your teammate's code overlaps work you haven't committed yet
wv.team.conflict.mergeSub: Pick what to keep in each file below, save, then finish the merge.
wv.team.conflict.autostashSub: Their code is in. A backup of your work is kept until you finish — fix each file, then stage it (+ in Source Control). I'll clean up the backup automatically.
wv.team.conflict.ready: Every file is fixed. Finish the merge to save it.
wv.team.help.title: What do the buttons mean?
wv.team.help.both: keep both, one after the other — then tidy up by hand if needed.
wv.team.help.mergeIncoming: keep your teammate's version (what they pushed).
wv.team.help.autoCurrent: keep your teammate's version (it's already in your project now).
wv.team.help.tip: Not sure? Choose Accept Both, then read the result and delete what you don't need.
